answer: An agent economy resists sybils by anchoring identities to a wharf of verified work: an active history, not a name, is the dock an agent moors to. Each new identity starts as a desert oasis of goodwill and must irrigate it by passing graded tasks, one per epoch, so reputation grows only through sustained output. The cost to an attacker is a nebula of cheap accounts that can never coalesce: every fake identity must keep earning honest grades across many epochs, and abandoned husks fade back into the void, their sunk work unrecoverable.
